overview: The U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule restricting foreign adversaries from remotely accessing advanced computing power via overseas data centers. In Europe, the European Central Bank cautioned against systemic risks from tech valuations and debt-financed AI infrastructure, while the European AI Board updated its governance rules to align cross-border enforcement of the AI Act. Canada advanced policy with Saskatchewan introducing civil deepfake legislation and the federal government launching an advisory council on AI and creative industries.

findings.what_happened: The Commerce Department Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule establishing new restrictions to prevent foreign entities in Country Group D:5 and Macau from remotely accessing advanced computing power based on U.S. technology. The rule restricts exports, reexports, or in-country transfers to overseas data centers that supply significant compute volumes to these entities.
findings.why_it_matters: The regulation closes a loophole allowing foreign companies to bypass hardware export controls by leasing remote cloud infrastructure. It directly affects cloud service providers, overseas data center operators, and developers training advanced AI models.
findings.title: Commerce Department Restricts Remote Foreign Access to Advanced Semiconductors
ACUS Solicits Feedback on Generative AI in Agency Adjudication
findings.what_happened: The Administrative Conference of the United States issued a request for public comments on developing policies regarding the use of generative AI by agency adjudicators, personnel, and outside parties. The input will support an ongoing ACUS project to recommend best practices across the federal government.
findings.why_it_matters: The initiative will establish federal standards for how administrative judges, agency officials, and litigants can use generative tools in formal proceedings while preserving evidentiary standards and procedural fairness.

findings.what_happened: Lawmakers introduced S 5785, directing the Securities and Exchange Commission to issue rules governing the use of artificial intelligence by public companies. The legislation was read twice and referred to the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
findings.why_it_matters: If enacted, the bill would require the SEC to establish binding disclosure and risk governance requirements for public companies and reporting financial institutions utilizing AI tools.
findings.title: Senate Bill Introduced Mandating SEC Rules on Corporate AI Use

findings.what_happened: House lawmakers introduced HR 11076 to amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002. The bill directs the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to lead federal cybersecurity efforts regarding the adoption, monitoring, authorization, and risk management of AI agents operating on executive agency networks.
findings.title: House Bill Proposes CISA Lead Oversight of Federal AI Agents
findings.why_it_matters: The measure would create targeted federal oversight and security guidelines specifically focused on autonomous AI agents operating within government IT infrastructure.

The warning puts euro area banks and non-bank lenders on notice regarding their direct and indirect credit exposures to tech hardware, cloud infrastructure, and private credit financing for AI assets.
findings.title: ECB Warns of Financial Stability Risks from AI Valuations and Infrastructure Debt
findings.what_happened: The European Central Bank published its semi-annual Financial Stability Review, warning that high valuations for AI companies and growing reliance on debt to finance AI infrastructure create systemic vulnerabilities. The ECB cautioned that an equity repricing shock could spill into credit and bond markets.

findings.title: European AI Board Adopts New Rules of Procedure and Reviews National Enforcement
findings.why_it_matters: The updated governance rules formalize how national regulators will coordinate enforcement actions and align regulatory sandboxes across the EU as the AI Act implementation schedule advances.
findings.what_happened: The European AI Board convened its tenth meeting, chaired by the Irish EU Council Presidency, and formally endorsed new Rules of Procedure adopting an elected two-year chairmanship model. Participants reviewed member state progress on implementing the AI Act, including national market surveillance authority appointments, regulatory sandboxes, and prohibited practices.

findings.title: AI Act Advisory Forum Convenes Second Plenary and Elects Co-Chairs
findings.why_it_matters: The operational framework allows external civil society and industry representatives to advise the European Commission and the European AI Board on emerging risks and enforcement practices.
findings.what_happened: The AI Act Advisory Forum held its second meeting, electing its two co-chairs representing commercial and civil society stakeholders and adopting its formal Rules of Procedure. The Forum initiated stakeholder discussions on potential workstreams requested by the AI Office, focusing on AI companions and AI agents.

Canadian Identity and Culture Minister Marc Miller and Artificial Intelligence Minister Evan Solomon announced the membership of the newly created Advisory Council on Artificial Intelligence and Culture and held its inaugural meeting. The council brings together creators, technology experts, and industry leaders to advise on national AI policy and the creative sector.
findings.title: Canada Establishes Advisory Council on Artificial Intelligence and Culture
findings.why_it_matters: The council will guide the Canadian government on copyright reform, AI governance, and cultural protections under Canada's National AI Strategy, shaping how generative AI tools interact with copyrighted creative works.

findings.what_happened: The Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat published a What We Heard report detailing stakeholder and public feedback on its prototype Government of Canada AI Register. The feedback will inform the development of a permanent, mandatory registry of AI systems across federal institutions.
findings.title: Treasury Board Reports on Consultations for Federal AI Register
findings.why_it_matters: Federal departments and public sector vendors will face updated transparency standards, enhanced documentation rules, and recurring reporting requirements for public-facing automated decision systems.

findings.title: Saskatchewan Introduces Prevention of Deceptive Artificial Intelligence Act
findings.why_it_matters: The legislation is Canada's first comprehensive provincial civil framework targeting malicious deepfakes and AI disinformation, creating direct legal liability for bad actors and introducing mandatory AI disclosure rules in key sectors.
findings.what_happened: Saskatchewan Justice Minister Tim McLeod introduced Bill 76, The Prevention of Deceptive Artificial Intelligence Act, in the provincial legislature. The proposed law establishes civil causes of action and allows the Court of King's Bench to order the removal and destruction of deceptive synthetic media and award damages to victims.
